A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 48 samples; 276 pool acquisition timeouts

report.summary: The restart at 03:26:28 cut the pool to 1 connection with a 250 ms timeout. An idle-in-transaction session then held a lock, so transfers timed out on acquisition (500/503) or ran slowly.

findings.claim: The 03:26:28 restart changed poolMaximumSize from 10 to 1 and poolConnectionTimeoutMs from 30000 to 250.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the changed settings, with a restart inside the window at 03:26:28.

findings.claim: The one-connection pool timed out on acquisition 276 times; pending borrowers and active connections were above zero from about 03:25:55 to 03:28:40.
findings.reason: Pool metrics show 276 acquisition timeouts, with maximum 1 and a 250 ms timeout.

findings.claim: A session idle in transaction blocked another ledger_app session for up to 1.9 s between 03:26:29 and 03:28:29, so the single connection stayed tied up and transfers failed or were slow.
findings.reason: The blocking starts just after the restart and overlaps the pool pressure. Transfers show 213 server errors of 586 (500×49, 503×164) and p95 of 1.6 s.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery is not the cause: all 390 deliveries succeeded in about 71 ms.
findings.reason: Every delivery attempt succeeded with fast timings.

limitations: Coverage is partial: a 10 s scrape gap at 03:26:20–03:26:30, 2 counter restarts, and gauges exported as NaN.
The idle-in-transaction session's origin and query were not identified, and the per-request error timing was not broken down.
